foundation_architecture.description: Complete 15-agent DAG architecture with 5 feature waves (FEAT-001 through FEAT-005)
agent_sequence: 01. Repository Auditor - Validates git repository state
02. Snapshot Authority - Generates snapshot and creates run directory
03. Evidence Freeze - Validates evidence structure from snapshot
04. Block Specification - Parses candidate structure and generates requirements
05. Candidate Intake - Validates package structure and computes hashes
06. Candidate Classification - Classifies block family with confidence scoring
07. Canonical Comparison - Compares with canonical artifacts
08. Placement Manifest - Generates placement manifest with hash
09. Human Approval - Database polling approval workflow (Governance)
10. Placement Executor - Executes approved placement manifest
11. Post-Placement Snapshot - Verifies placement using git diff
12. Certification Controller - Orchestrates all certification gates
13. Runtime Agent (12K) - Verifies blocks at runtime by starting application
14. Playwright Browser Agent (12L) - Orchestrates Node Playwright browser tests
15. Human Certification - Final human certification with database polling

verification_modules.notes: Foundation adds dependency.py for dependency graph verification (circular dependencies, version conflicts, unlicensed packages). Canonical-wiring has browser_verifier.py and runtime_verifier.py which foundation integrates into agents.

foundation_architecture.gate_orchestration: Agent 12 (Certification Controller) orchestrates all gates as methods, not separate modules

certification_gates.notes: Foundation consolidates gate execution into gates.py with modifications (214 additions). Canonical-wiring has separate browser_verification.py and runtime_verification.py modules.

evidence_systems.notes: Canonical-wiring has 4 additional evidence modules. Foundation modified logger.py (14 additions) but removed or consolidated canonical_evidence.py, integration.py, ledger.py, and schemas.py.

data_models.notes: Foundation adds 5 DAG-specific models (agent_result, certification, gate_result, placement, specification). Canonical-wiring has implementation_approval, workflow, and workflow_target models.

orchestration.notes: Foundation adds workflow_dag.py (191 lines) defining the 15-agent DAG structure. Canonical-wiring has canonical_workflow.py and workflow_governance.py. Both branches heavily modified core orchestration files.

test_files.notes: Foundation adds 13 new agent tests for DAG-specific agents plus 1 DAG execution test and 1 full workflow integration test. Canonical-wiring has more integration tests covering implementation_approval, placement_engine, repositories, restart persistence, security, and contract generation.

database_schema.notes: Foundation adds database schema for approval_requests table and certification_reviews table to support human-in-loop approval (Agent 09) and certification (Agent 15) workflows with database polling.

documentation.notes: Foundation includes extensive documentation for the 15-agent DAG design, 5 feature waves (FEAT-001 to FEAT-005), design reviews, verdicts, and phase 2 completion report.

helper_scripts.notes: Foundation includes Python helper scripts to fix gate test issues during development.

foundation.architecture: 15-agent DAG with explicit dependencies and parallel execution groups
foundation.orchestration: workflow_dag.py defines agent sequence and dependencies
foundation.human_in_loop: Two database-polling human gates (Agent 09 Approval, Agent 15 Certification)
foundation.verification: Dedicated Runtime Agent (12K) and Playwright Browser Agent (12L)
foundation.evidence: Evidence Freeze (Agent 03) validates snapshot evidence structure
foundation.snapshot: Snapshot Authority (Agent 02) generates snapshot once, frozen for workflow
foundation.repository_validation: Repository Auditor (Agent 01) validates git state before workflow
foundation.approval_workflow: Approval agent polls approval_requests table with manifest_hash validation
foundation.certification_workflow: Human Certification agent polls certification_reviews table
foundation.placement: Separate Placement Manifest (08) and Placement Executor (10) agents
foundation.classification: Dedicated Classification agent (06) with confidence scoring
foundation.dependency_verification: Dependency verification in verification/dependency.py with circular dependency detection

canonical_wiring.architecture: Agent registry with workflow engine coordination
canonical_wiring.verification: Separate browser_verification.py and runtime_verification.py modules in certification/
canonical_wiring.evidence: Evidence modules include canonical_evidence, integration, ledger, schemas
canonical_wiring.certification_workflow: Final gate certification without separate human review agent

foundation_requires: Node Playwright installed and configured with playwright.project-ai.config.ts
pnpm workspace with TypeScript discovery script at .agents/scripts/regenerate-m1-snapshot.mjs
Git repository with clean working directory
Evidence directory structure for frozen evidence baseline

conflicts_expected: final_gate.py and intake.py modified in both branches
architectural_decision_required: Decide on human-in-loop approach: database polling (foundation) vs implementation approval (canonical-wiring)
Evidence system: frozen baseline (foundation) vs ledger/integration (canonical-wiring)
Verification architecture: dedicated agents (foundation) vs separate modules (canonical-wiring)
Model structure: DAG-specific models (foundation) vs workflow models (canonical-wiring)
incompatible_features: agent_result.py, gate_result.py, certification.py models (foundation) vs implementation_approval.py, workflow.py models (canonical-wiring)
approval.py + human_certification.py polling agents (foundation) vs governance-based approval (canonical-wiring)
Evidence freeze + snapshot authority agents (foundation) vs integrated snapshot generation (canonical-wiring)

recommendation.reason: Foundation implements a complete 15-agent DAG architecture with 111,854 lines added across 9 commits. Canonical-wiring has a different orchestration model. Merging would require choosing one architecture and discarding the other, not reconciling both.
alternatives: Option 1: Merge canonical-wiring to main, keep foundation as experimental DAG branch
Option 2: Merge foundation to main if DAG architecture is the chosen direction, cherry-pick needed canonical-wiring features
Option 3: Create foundation-v2 branch that incorporates desired canonical-wiring features into the DAG architecture
